why: Correct and unambiguous, but a five-word A2-style frame (the card's own watch line is *I [[know]] the answer*) with A2 distractors (*not know, doesn't know*); too easy for B1.1, keep for practice.
It repeats the card's example (present_simple card: "Water [[boils]] at 100 degrees."), is an A2 fact at B1.1, and *is boil* is a form nobody writes; nothing B1 to keep without a new task.
One clear mistake (*is owning*, a real learner error; card: "State verbs ... stay simple"); the three right sentences are about different things.
No instruction stem and quoted options; *I wanted a coffee now* is an odd, half-correct sentence (polite past *I wanted a coffee* is English). Ask *Which sentence is correct?* and drop it.

fix.correct: I want a coffee.
wrong: I'm wanting a coffee.
I am want a coffee.
fix.why: *want* is a state verb, so it stays simple: *I want a coffee.*
fix.why_lv: *want* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds, tāpēc paliek Present Simple: *I want a coffee.*

why: Reader is right: without a past time, *She opens the door and walks in* (and the perfect) also describe the order. A time word decides it.

fix.q: Choose the correct option: Yesterday she ___ the door and walked in.
fix.correct: opened
wrong: was opening
has opened
opens
fix.why: A series of finished actions in the past (*yesterday*): past simple: *Yesterday she opened the door and walked in.*
fix.why_lv: Pabeigtu darbību virkne pagātnē (*yesterday*): Past Simple: *Yesterday she opened the door and walked in.*

why: Gate card_words: *from* (and *ago*) are not on the present_perfect card, which teaches "*[[for]]* + a period, *[[since]]* + a starting point" and signals "ever, never, just, already, yet, for, since". Use *already* (the Latvian *jau piecus gadus* mistake) instead.

wrong: since
already
fix.why: *for* + a period of time: *I've worked here for five years.* *since* + a starting point (*since 2020*). *already* does not go before a period of time.
fix.why_lv: *for* + laika posms: *I've worked here for five years.* *since* + sākuma brīdis (*since 2020*). *already* nelieto pirms laika posma.

why: Reader agrees with the key; *We booked a table yesterday* rules out *I'll meet*; one answer.
The first sentence spells out the logic (superfluous, gives the answer away); *although* is not on the cond_first card (signals "if, unless, as soon as, when, in case").

fix.q: Choose the correct option: We won't finish on time ___ we start now.
fix.correct: unless
wrong: if
when
fix.why: *Unless* = *if ... not*: *We won't finish on time unless we start now* (= if we don't start now).
fix.why_lv: *Unless* = *if ... not*: *We won't finish on time unless we start now* (= ja nesāksim tūlīt).

why: Gate mistake: the right sentences are near-copies of the wrong one. Three right sentences about different things.

wrong: She would travel more if she didn't have a dog.
What would you say if your boss offered you a promotion?
If we had a garden, we could grow vegetables.

why: Gate mistake (near-copies), the odd *If I hadn't known...*, and the wrong sentence is the cond_third card's own mistake ("If I [[would have known]], I would have called."). New mistake sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: If I would have seen the message, I would have replied.
wrong: If it hadn't rained, we would have eaten outside.
She wouldn't have got lost if she had taken a map.
What would you have done if the bank had said no?
fix.why: Do not use *would* in the if-part: *If I had seen the message, I would have replied.*
fix.why_lv: *If* daļā nelieto *would*: *If I had seen the message, I would have replied.*

why: Gate mistake (near-copies); the wrong sentence is also almost the rep_statements card mistake ("He [[said me]] that he was tired."). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: She said me that the meeting was cancelled.
wrong: He told us he had found a new job.
They said they would call back later.
Anna told me she was moving abroad.
fix.why: After *said* we do not put a person directly: *She told me that the meeting was cancelled* or *She said to me that ...*
fix.why_lv: Pēc *said* personu tieši nelieto: *She told me that the meeting was cancelled* vai *She said to me that ...*

why: Gate mistake: *We visited the Old Town last summer* is a near-copy; only three options. Three right sentences about different things (articles_b1 card: meals, languages, mountain ranges).

wrong: My sister is learning Italian.
We had lunch near the river.
They went skiing in the Alps.
fix.why: Cities take no article: *We visited Riga last summer.*
fix.why_lv: Pilsētām artikulu nelieto: *We visited Riga last summer.*

why: Gate card_words: *Unless, Because, Until* are not on the cond_zero card (signals "if, when, whenever, every time"), and *When* also fits; the sentence copies the card use "If you [[mix]] red and blue, you [[get]] purple." Test the card's point, the verb form.

fix.q: Choose the correct option: If you leave milk out of the fridge all day, it ___ sour.
fix.correct: goes
wrong: went
would go
fix.why: A general truth: present simple in both parts: *If you leave milk out of the fridge all day, it goes sour.*
fix.why_lv: Vispārīga patiesība: abās daļās Present Simple: *If you leave milk out of the fridge all day, it goes sour.*

why: Gate card_words: *unless, so, although* are not on the cond_zero card (signals "if, when, whenever, every time"); readers note *when / whenever* also fit. Test the verb form in the if-part instead (card mistake "If you [[will heat]] ice").

fix.q: Choose the correct option: I get a headache if I ___ too much coffee.
fix.correct: drink
wrong: will drink
drank
fix.why: A general truth: present simple in both parts, no *will*: *I get a headache if I drink too much coffee.*
fix.why_lv: Vispārīga patiesība: abās daļās Present Simple, bez *will*: *I get a headache if I drink too much coffee.*

why: Gate mistake: all four sentences are the same click/page sentence; reader notes polite *If you will click here* exists. Use a subject where *will* can only be the mistake, and three different right sentences.

fix.correct: If the battery will get low, the screen goes dark.
wrong: My cat hides when it hears thunder.
If people don't drink enough water, they get headaches.
We eat outside when the weather is warm.
fix.why: In a general truth the *if*-part uses the present simple, not *will*: *If the battery gets low, the screen goes dark.*
fix.why_lv: Vispārīgā patiesībā *if* daļā lieto Present Simple, nevis *will*: *If the battery gets low, the screen goes dark.*

why: Gate card_words: *so, than* are not on the cond_first card (signals "if, unless, as soon as, when, in case"); the sentence is also the card's own example ("[[Unless]] you hurry, you'll miss the bus."). New sentence, card words only; *until* avoided because it would fit.

fix.q: Choose the correct option: They won't let you in ___ you show your ticket.
fix.correct: unless
wrong: if
when
as soon as
fix.why: *Unless* = *if ... not*: *They won't let you in unless you show your ticket* (= if you don't show it).
fix.why_lv: *Unless* = *if ... not*: *They won't let you in unless you show your ticket* (= ja neparādīsi biļeti).

why: Gate mistake: the three right sentences are copies of the wrong one. Three right sentences about different things.

wrong: If I were you, I would take the job.
They would visit us more often if we lived closer.
Would you move abroad if you had the chance?

why: Gate mistake (near-copies); it repeated 011's mistake and the card use ("If I [[had studied]], I [[would have passed]]."). New mistake (a real one: *had* + past form), three different right sentences.

fix.correct: If she had knew about the party, she would have come.
wrong: They would have won if their best player hadn't been injured.
Would you have helped me if I had asked?
If the shop had been open, I would have bought some bread.
fix.why: After *had* we need the 3. form: *If she had known about the party, she would have come.*
fix.why_lv: Pēc *had* vajag 3. formu: *If she had known about the party, she would have come.*

why: Gate mistake (near-copies), the odd *we'd have caught it*, and the sentence is the cond_third card's example ("If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train."). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: If he had booked earlier, he wouldn't have pay so much.
wrong: If I had seen the sign, I would have stopped.
She would have called you if she had had your number.
If you hadn't reminded me, I would have forgotten her birthday.
fix.why: After *wouldn't have* we need the 3. form: *If he had booked earlier, he wouldn't have paid so much.*
fix.why_lv: Pēc *wouldn't have* vajag 3. formu: *If he had booked earlier, he wouldn't have paid so much.*

why: Gate card_words: *many* is not on the articles_b1 card ("No article ... *the*: a particular one"; watch "She plays [[the]] piano") and is another kind of word. Replace it with *—* (no article), as the topic's other tasks do ("— | A").
Gate mistake (*He lives in the Netherlands* is a near-copy) and the wrong sentence is the card's own mistake ("He lives in [[the Latvia]]."). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: My parents moved to the Canada last year.
wrong: She works in the Netherlands.
We had breakfast on the balcony.
We took a boat trip on the Danube.
fix.why: No article with most countries: *My parents moved to Canada last year.* But: *the Netherlands, the UK*.
fix.why_lv: Ar lielāko daļu valstu nosaukumu artikula nav: *My parents moved to Canada last year.* Bet: *the Netherlands, the UK*.

why: Gate mistake: the right sentences are copies (*... time for hobbies*). Three right sentences about different things, quantity-card words only.

wrong: There aren't many shops in our village.
Would you like some more coffee?
We have a little time before the train leaves.

why: Gate mistake (near-copies); *My sister who lives in Paris* is correct but confusing; the wrong sentence is almost the card's mistake ("My brother, [[that]] lives in Berlin, is a nurse."). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: Our new manager, that started in May, is from Spain.
wrong: The hotel where we stayed was right next to the beach.
I have a friend whose father is a pilot.
Riga, which is the capital of Latvia, has a beautiful old town.
fix.why: Extra information about a person we already know goes between commas, with *who*, never *that*: *Our new manager, who started in May, is from Spain.*
fix.why_lv: Papildu informācija par jau zināmu cilvēku ir starp komatiem, ar *who*, nekad ar *that*: *Our new manager, who started in May, is from Spain.*

why: Gate mistake (near-copies); *after I will have spoken* is a form learners rarely write. Use the card's real mistake type ("when I [[will arrive]]") in a new sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: Let's wait here until the rain will stop.
wrong: I'll call you after I've spoken to the manager.
Please lock the door before you leave.
While I'm away, my sister will water the plants.
fix.why: After *until* (and *when, as soon as, before, after*) we use the present simple for the future, not *will*: *Let's wait here until the rain stops.*
fix.why_lv: Pēc *until* (un *when, as soon as, before, after*) nākotnei lieto Present Simple, nevis *will*: *Let's wait here until the rain stops.*

why: Gate mistake (near-copy) and the reader's level flag: tags after *ought to* and *had better* are not on the question_tags card ("*is / are / was / were, have / has, can, will, should* ... *do / does / did*"). Use the card's own mistake type ("You like tea, [[isn't it]]?").

fix.correct: Your brother lives in Oslo, isn't he?
wrong: You can drive, can't you?
They weren't at the party, were they?
Let's take a break, shall we?
fix.why: Present simple: the tag uses *doesn't*: *Your brother lives in Oslo, doesn't he?*
fix.why_lv: Present Simple: tag ar *doesn't*: *Your brother lives in Oslo, doesn't he?*

why: Gate example: the explanation uses *Remember to take it* / *seeing it*. *to see* is no answer here (*for the first time* makes it a memory). New explanation with the task's sentence.

fix.why: *forget* + *-ing* = a memory of something you did: *I'll never forget seeing the Eiffel Tower for the first time.* *forget* + *to* = something you must do.
fix.why_lv: *forget* + *-ing* = atmiņa par to, ko izdarīji: *I'll never forget seeing the Eiffel Tower for the first time.* *forget* + *to* = kaut kas, kas jāizdara.

why: The reader's flag is rejected: *Rewrite with forgot* is a rewrite task, the change is the task (copy rule exemption), and the learner still has to choose *to lock*. Gate example: the explanation's *I'll never forget seeing it* is from another task; new explanation.

fix.why: *forget* + *to* = something you had to do and did not do: *I forgot to lock the door.* *forget* + *-ing* is a memory of something you did.
fix.why_lv: *forget* + *to* = kaut kas, kas bija jāizdara, bet netika izdarīts: *I forgot to lock the door.* *forget* + *-ing* ir atmiņa par to, ko izdarīji.

why: Gate mistake (near-copies) and the sentence is the passive_modals card's example ("Tickets can be bought online."). New sentence with the card's mistake type ("The report [[must finished]] today"), three different right ones.

fix.correct: This medicine should taken after meals.
wrong: The bill can be paid by card.
Your passport must be shown at the gate.
This room can't be used during the exam.
fix.why: modal + *be* + 3. form: *This medicine should be taken after meals.*
fix.why_lv: modālais darbības vārds + *be* + 3. forma: *This medicine should be taken after meals.*

why: Gate mistake: the three right sentences are copies about the shoes. Three different right ones; explanation with the task's own sentence.

wrong: The meeting might be moved to Friday.
Can this jacket be washed at home?
The plants have to be watered every day.
fix.why: modal + *be* + 3. form, also after *ought to*: *The shoes ought to be taken off.*
fix.why_lv: modālais darbības vārds + *be* + 3. forma, arī pēc *ought to*: *The shoes ought to be taken off.*

why: Gate card_words: *in* (and *at*) are not taught on the two_objects card ("*to*: give, send ... *for*: buy, make ..."); the sentence is also the card's own example ("*She explained the problem to me.*"). New sentence with *introduce* (on the card), bank *to / for / —*.

fix.q: She introduced her new colleague ___ the whole team.
fix.why: *explain, suggest, describe, introduce*: first the thing or the person you introduce, then *to* + person: *She introduced her new colleague to the whole team.*
fix.why_lv: *explain, suggest, describe, introduce*: vispirms lieta vai cilvēks, ko iepazīstina, tad *to* + persona: *She introduced her new colleague to the whole team.*

why: Gate card_words: *in* (and *at, of*) are not on the two_objects card, which teaches *to* vs *for* ("I bought a present [[to]] my sister" is its mistake). Use *for* and *—*.

wrong: for
fix.why: *lend* + thing + *to* + person: *He lent his car to his neighbour* (= *He lent his neighbour his car*). *for* goes with *buy, make, cook*.
fix.why_lv: *lend* + lieta + *to* + persona: *He lent his car to his neighbour* (= *He lent his neighbour his car*). *for* lieto ar *buy, make, cook*.

why: Gate mistake (near-copies) and the sentence is the adj_order card's example ("a beautiful small black leather bag"). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: She wore a cotton white dress.
wrong: We sat at a big round table.
He drives a small Japanese car.
I found a beautiful wooden box.
fix.why: Colour before material: *She wore a white cotton dress.* Order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material.
fix.why_lv: Krāsa pirms materiāla: *She wore a white cotton dress.* Secība: viedoklis, izmērs, vecums, forma, krāsa, izcelsme, materiāls.

why: Gate example: the explanation's table phrase is not this task. The instruction is acceptable (the labels name what is matched); new explanation with the task's own words.

fix.why: *huge* = size, *round* = shape, *Spanish* = origin, *silk* = material. Before a noun the order is: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material.
fix.why_lv: *huge* = izmērs, *round* = forma, *Spanish* = izcelsme, *silk* = materiāls. Pirms lietvārda secība ir: viedoklis, izmērs, vecums, forma, krāsa, izcelsme, materiāls.

why: Gate card_words: *very* is not on the card (so_such card: "*so* + adjective or adverb", "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun", "*so much / so many* + noun", mistakes "It was [[so a]] long film", "There were [[so much]] people"; *very* and *too* are not on it.); the sentence is the card's example ("It was such a long film"). New sentence, bank from the card.

fix.q: We had ___ a lovely evening at your place yesterday.
fix.why: *such* + *a* + adjective + noun: *We had such a lovely evening.* *so* goes before an adjective with no noun.
fix.why_lv: *such* + *a* + īpašības vārds + lietvārds: *We had such a lovely evening.* *so* lieto pirms īpašības vārda bez lietvārda.

why: Gate card_words: *too* is not on the card (so_such card: "*so* + adjective or adverb", "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun", "*so much / so many* + noun", mistakes "It was [[so a]] long film", "There were [[so much]] people"; *very* and *too* are not on it.); the sentence nearly copies the card use "I was [[so tired that]] I fell asleep at once", and *so ... that* is a B1.2 point in the map. New B1.1 sentence.

fix.q: Thank you for your help. You've been ___ kind.
fix.why: *so* + adjective with no noun: *You've been so kind.* *such (a)* needs a noun.
fix.why_lv: *so* + īpašības vārds bez lietvārda: *You've been so kind.* *such (a)* vajag lietvārdu.

why: Gate card_words: *very* is not on the card (so_such card: "*so* + adjective or adverb", "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun", "*so much / so many* + noun", mistakes "It was [[so a]] long film", "There were [[so much]] people"; *very* and *too* are not on it.); *so much noise* is the card's example. New sentence, bank from the card.

fix.q: There was ___ much traffic that we were late for the wedding.
fix.why: *so much* + uncountable noun: *There was so much traffic that we were late for the wedding.*
fix.why_lv: *so much* + neskaitāms lietvārds: *There was so much traffic that we were late for the wedding.*

why: Gate card_words: *very* is not on the card (so_such card: "*so* + adjective or adverb", "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun", "*so much / so many* + noun", mistakes "It was [[so a]] long film", "There were [[so much]] people"; *very* and *too* are not on it.). Replace it with *so much*; the sentence and the explanation stay.

Gate card_words: *too* is not on the card (so_such card: "*so* + adjective or adverb", "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun", "*so much / so many* + noun", mistakes "It was [[so a]] long film", "There were [[so much]] people"; *very* and *too* are not on it.); reader: duplicate of 036 and near the card use. New B1.1 sentence without the B1.2 *that* result.

fix.q: Choose the correct option: The hotel staff were ___ friendly to us.
fix.correct: so
wrong: such
such a
so many
fix.why: *so* + adjective with no noun: *The hotel staff were so friendly to us.*
fix.why_lv: *so* + īpašības vārds bez lietvārda: *The hotel staff were so friendly to us.*

why: Gate card_words: *very* is not on the card (so_such card: "*so* + adjective or adverb", "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun", "*so much / so many* + noun", mistakes "It was [[so a]] long film", "There were [[so much]] people"; *very* and *too* are not on it.); reader: duplicate of 035. Let the learner place *a* (card: "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun").

fix.q: Choose the correct option: It was ___ surprise to see him at the party.
fix.correct: such a
wrong: so
such
so a
fix.why: *such a* + singular noun: *It was such a surprise to see him at the party.*
fix.why_lv: *such a* + vienskaitļa lietvārds: *It was such a surprise to see him at the party.*

why: Gate card_words: *very* is not on the card (so_such card: "*so* + adjective or adverb", "*such* + (*a / an*) + (adjective) + noun", "*so much / so many* + noun", mistakes "It was [[so a]] long film", "There were [[so much]] people"; *very* and *too* are not on it.). Replace it with *so much*.

wrong: such
such a
so much

why: Gate mistake: *Three people have been arrested* is a near-copy. Three right sentences about different things.

wrong: The road has been closed since Monday.
Has your bike been repaired yet?
My wallet has been stolen!

why: Gate mistake: the right sentences copy the wrong one. Three different right sentences.

wrong: Your new card will be sent to you by post.
Will the museum be closed on Monday?
The match won't be shown on TV.

why: Gate mistake (near-copies) and the sentence is the future_passive card's mistake ("The results [[will announced]] on Friday"). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: The new library will opened next spring.
wrong: The road will be repaired in August.
Will lunch be served on the plane?
The old bridge won't be used any more.
fix.why: We need *be*: *The new library will be opened next spring.*
fix.why_lv: Vajag *be*: *The new library will be opened next spring.*

why: Gate mistake: three copies of the *When I came in* sentence. Three different right sentences (not the card's *I was cooking when the phone rang*).

wrong: She was driving to work when the accident happened.
What were you doing at eight last night?
It wasn't raining when we left the house.

why: Gate card_words: *from* (and *ago*) are not on the present_perfect card; reader: near-duplicate of 007. Test *since* instead; *in 2019* is the card's mistake type (a finished time: "I [[have seen]] him yesterday").

fix.q: Choose the correct option: She has worked here ___ 2019.
fix.correct: since
wrong: for
in
fix.why: *since* + a starting point: *She has worked here since 2019.* *for* goes with a period of time. *in 2019* is a finished time and needs the past simple.
fix.why_lv: *since* + sākuma brīdis: *She has worked here since 2019.* *for* lieto ar laika posmu. *in 2019* ir pabeigts laiks, tam vajag Past Simple.

why: Gate mistake (near-copy) and the wrong sentence is the card's own mistake ("I [[have been knowing]] him for years."). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: She's been knowing about the problem for weeks.
wrong: They've been learning Spanish since January.
How long have you been waiting?
We've owned this flat since 2015.
fix.why: *Know* is a state verb: *She's known about the problem for weeks.*
fix.why_lv: *Know* ir stāvokļa darbības vārds: *She's known about the problem for weeks.*

why: Gate mistake (near-copies) and the sentence nearly copies the card's mistake ("She has been [[work]] all day."). New sentence, three different right ones.

fix.correct: My neighbour has been build a garage all summer.
wrong: It has been snowing for two days.
How long have you been learning to drive?
They've been living in Riga for two years.
fix.why: After *been* the verb needs *-ing*: *My neighbour has been building a garage all summer.*
fix.why_lv: Pēc *been* darbības vārdam vajag *-ing*: *My neighbour has been building a garage all summer.*

why: *left* is right (past simple with clock times; *had left* is not offered and not needed). But *was leaving* can be read as a past plan; replace it with a clearly wrong form.

wrong: leaving
has left
is leaving

why: Gate card_words: *very, too* are not on the comparison card; but the card's *a lot / a bit / slightly* would all fit the gap. Put *more* into the options so only one fits: *much* alone and *the most* (card: "the most") are wrong before *than*.

fix.q: Choose the correct option: The new hotel is ___ comfortable than the old one, so we will stay there again.
fix.correct: much more
wrong: much
the most
fix.why: *much* + comparative shows a big difference: *much more comfortable than the old one*. *the most* compares one with all the others.
fix.why_lv: *much* + pārākā pakāpe parāda lielu atšķirību: *much more comfortable than the old one*. *the most* salīdzina vienu ar visiem pārējiem.

why: Gate mistake: three copies of *... work late*. Three different right sentences (not the card's *You mustn't park here*).

wrong: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.
Did you have to wear a uniform at school?
We don't have to pay for parking on Sundays.

why: Gate card_words: *enough of* is not on the quantity card ("*enough* + noun: *enough chairs*"). Use *much* (card: "*many* + plural ... *much* + uncountable"). After the fix it is still an A2.2 point (map: "Too, too much, too many, enough"); it may be practice only.

wrong: too much
much

why: Gate card_words: *enough of* is not on the quantity card ("*enough* + noun"). Use *many*.

wrong: too many
many
fix.why: *enough* + uncountable noun: *There isn't enough flour.* *many* goes with plurals.
fix.why_lv: *enough* + neskaitāms lietvārds: *There isn't enough flour.* *many* lieto ar daudzskaitli.

why: Gate card_words: *very few* (and *very little*) are not on the quantity card, which teaches "*few / little* (without *a*) = almost none" and the mistake "I have [[a few]] money".

fix.correct: little
wrong: few
a few
fix.why: *little* (without *a*) + uncountable noun = almost none: *I've got little money.* *few* goes with plurals.
fix.why_lv: *little* (bez *a*) + neskaitāms lietvārds = gandrīz nemaz: *I've got little money.* *few* lieto ar daudzskaitli.
